label: No sex allocation is uninvadable unless investment in the two sexes is equal
statement_en: For a rare mutant parent with resource R > 0 splitting fraction x into sons (cost cs > 0 each) and the rest into daughters (cost cd > 0 each) in a population of Nm > 0 males and Nd > 0 females, with Shaw-Mohler fitness wAlloc(x) = (1-x)*R/cd + x*R*Nd/(cs*Nm) (a named hypothesis): if cs*Nm < cd*Nd then fitness strictly increases in x so a more male-biased parent strictly invades; if cd*Nd < cs*Nm then a more female-biased parent strictly invades; and only when cs*Nm = cd*Nd does every allocation do equally well. Hence no sex allocation is uninvadable unless total investment in the two sexes is equal, of which the 1:1 ratio is the special case cs = cd.

hypotheses.name: Delphi.LeanBio.Round2.SexRatio.SexRatioHyp
hypotheses.statement: A rare mutant parent's relative fitness is the Shaw-Mohler form wAlloc(x) = (1-x)*R/cd + x*R*Nd/(cs*Nm), with resource R > 0, per-son cost cs > 0, per-daughter cost cd > 0, and a population containing Nm > 0 males and Nd > 0 females. Offspring of each sex are weighted by the reproductive value of that sex, which is inversely proportional to its number.
hypotheses.source: Fisher RA (1930) The Genetical Theory of Natural Selection, ch. 6 (book, no DOI); Shaw RF, Mohler JD (1953) The selective significance of the sex ratio. American Naturalist 87:337-342, doi:10.1086/281794 (recorded as see_also on the claim); claim notation in math-bio-theorems/claims/key-claims.json (fisher-sex-ratio)

scope.basis: Panmixia, autosomal control of the sex ratio, each offspring with one father and one mother, no local mate competition and no sex-specific resource competition. Says nothing when offspring of the two sexes do not compete at random: under local mate competition the stable ratio is female-biased (Hamilton's LMC, claim hamilton-lmc in this repo), and this law does not apply there. Nor does it establish that any population sits at equal investment.

browser_check.relation: cs Nm = cd Nd  (equal total investment in the two sexes; the only uninvadable allocation)
browser_check.note: Checks a design that CLAIMS its sex allocation is evolutionarily stable. 'violated' means some allocation strictly invades, so the stability claim is refuted - it does not mean the organism is impossible, since a population can sit away from equal investment for any number of reasons. The row is a false positive for any species under local mate competition, where the stable ratio is female-biased; such a design is out of this law's scope rather than in violation of it, and must be excluded by scope before this row is read.

browser_check_caveat.reason: The operator and direction were checked: the law's content is an impossibility (nothing but equality is uninvadable), so an equality row with 'violated' meaning 'a stability claim is refuted' is the right shape. But a sim-engine design has no sex counts and no per-offspring costs; sim-engine/lib/state.mjs and perturb-map.mjs carry morphology, thermal, hydrostatic and metabolic fields only. The row will read cannot-evaluate for every design we can currently write.

sources: Fisher RA (1930) The Genetical Theory of Natural Selection, ch. 6
